56/S0.subgoal: Explain why computer graphics is needed to understand rendering and resource optimization in VR.

56/S1.subgoal: Describe the five stages of the 3D graphics pipeline and identify the stages covered in this lecture.

56/S2.subgoal: Explain the purpose of modeling transformation and identify the basic transformations used to place local-coordinate objects into a world scene.

56/S3.subgoal: Describe how transformations are represented by homogeneous-coordinate matrices and how a local point is transformed to a world point.

56/S4.subgoal: Explain how composite transformation matrices are formed and applied in a worked example to obtain transformed vertices.

56/S5.subgoal: Explain the role of color computation in the pipeline, including the distinction between lighting and shading models and the continuous intensity values used by lighting models.

56/S6.subgoal: Describe how light is emitted, reflected, and perceived as color, and introduce the simple lighting model as the sum of ambient, diffuse, and specular components.

56/S7.subgoal: Explain how the ambient, diffuse, and specular components are computed using reflection coefficients and vector dot products.

56/S8.subgoal: Explain how radial and angular intensity attenuation modify the simple lighting model.

56/S9.subgoal: Describe how colored light sources and multiple light sources extend the lighting model.

56/S10.subgoal: Explain how continuous lighting-model intensities are mapped to finite device-supported intensity values and bit patterns.

56/S11.subgoal: Summarize the main points of the lecture.
